howDoI.q: How do I let the player start a level over?
How do I make a pit too deep to climb out of?
How do I give the player a ladder out of a pit?
How do I make steps the player can jump up through?
How do I make steps out of solid blocks?
How do I put the player back at the way in?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Try Again is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: A Post to Start Over
pages.html:
Level 1: A Post to Start Over

TOO DEEP TO CLIMB OUT. JUMP IT comes first, then A POST AT THE BOTTOM STARTS THE LEVEL OVER. Ahead is a pit four blocks deep, with four coins over it and a coin and a post at the bottom. Jump across it, or fall in on purpose.

If you fall in, Mia cannot jump out: she jumps a little over three blocks. Walk to the post and touch it. The level starts over, with Mia back at the way in and the coin back in the pit. THE LEVEL IS NEW AGAIN. YOUR SCORE STAYS stands past the pit.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The pit. Open one.map in the map editor. The pit is four columns where the grass and the dirt below it are replaced by open sky, four rows deep. The floor under it is the dirt that is left. Mia's jump is a little over three blocks, so a four-block wall is one she cannot jump out of.
  • The post. Open mt.bbl in the blocks editor and pick post. It is an ordinary block: not solid, and nothing happens on its Touch tab. It is only a picture of a post.
  • The link. What makes it start the level over is in mt.gam. Open it in the integrator and select the scene A Post to Start Over. It has two links: one from the door at the end to the next scene, and one that starts at the post's square and leads back to this same scene, with Mia put back at the way in. A link fires when Mia touches the square it starts at, and the level is loaded again from the map file.
  • What comes back. Everything on the map starts as it was: coins, blocks that were touched and changed. Mia's score stays, as the bot that plays this game checks.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door at the end to the next level.

pages.head: Level 2: Ways Back
pages.html:
Level 2: Ways Back

LET THEM FALL. GIVE THEM A WAY BACK comes first. Three pits follow, each four blocks deep, each with a coin at the bottom and each with its own way out: A LADDER IS A WAY BACK, then PLANKS ARE STEPS YOU JUMP UP THROUGH, then SO ARE SOLID BLOCKS.

Jump the pits, or go down for the coin and climb out again. There is no post here, because nobody can be stuck. The three coins are worth thirty points.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The ladder. Open two.map in the map editor. A column of ladder runs from the floor of the first pit up to the level of the ground, one block higher than the grass. Hold Up on it to climb, then walk off the top.
  • The planks. In the second pit one plank is two blocks wide a little way up, and another is level with the ground. A plank is solid only from above: Mia jumps up through it from below and lands on it. Each step is two blocks, which she can jump.
  • The solid blocks. In the third pit two columns of dirt make a staircase, one block and then two blocks high, and then the last jump is up onto the ground. These are solid on every side, so Mia stands on them and cannot jump through them.
  • Why a step has to be small. Mia's jump is a little over three blocks, so no step is higher than two. If a pit had a wall of four blocks and no step, it would be a trap, and it would need a post.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door to the The End scene.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • There is no restart key. A post is a place on the map. A scene link starts at one square, so Mia has to walk there and touch it. A player who is far from a post cannot use it, and a player who is stuck somewhere with no post cannot start over: put a post wherever they can get stuck, or give them a way back so they cannot.
  • One square, one link. A link fires from one block, the square the post stands in. A second post needs a second link. A scene has room for a fixed number of links, and the exit uses one.
  • It starts the whole level over. There is no checkpoint in the middle of a level: the map is loaded again, and Mia goes where the link says. The coins come back too, so a coin is worth ten points each time. Keep that in mind if the coins are worth anything to your game.
  • Only the map starts over. The score stays, as Mia's counters belong to her and not to the scene. The link cannot choose which counters to keep.
  • It cannot tell a trap from a puzzle. A pit with no way back looks the same to the Level check as a pit with one. It cannot see that a player is stuck, so play your own levels and try to get stuck.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Move the post to the far end of the pit, or put a second pit in the level with a post of its own.
  • In the integrator, change where the post's link puts Mia back, to the middle of the level.
  • Add a block to the second step of the planks so it is too high to jump.
  • Make the ladder one block shorter so it stops short of the ground.
  • Draw a new picture for the post.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
